name: Homunculus
soul: The soul of one who was told what they were for, and has been deciding for themselves ever since.
spark: The mote copies you. A beat late and a little wrong, it does what your hands just did.

hybrid.text: Somebody made it and did not finish. It has been finishing itself ever since, from watching.

settled.name: Unfinished Homunculus
settled.text: Clay to the knees and unfinished above, with your thumbprint still in its forehead. It watches your hands as if they were the only book.
settled.sign: Clay to the knees and rough above, with your thumbprint still in its forehead.
settled.habit: It copies whatever your hands do, a beat late, with nothing in its own.

paths.name: Clay Apprentice
paths.of: one who cannot leave a thing half-made
paths.text: It learned from you that a thing left half-made nags. It does what you do, and then the next thing, before you have got to it.
paths.sign: Clay under its nails and a brush behind its ear. Its fingers are better finished than the rest of it.
paths.habit: It finishes things you put down: a knot, a sentence, the last of your tea.

prongs.name: Copy-clerk
prongs.of: one who writes it all down, in a better hand than their teacher's
prongs.text: It keeps your notes, and has started keeping its own, in a hand much better than yours.
prongs.sign: Ink to the wrists, a pen behind each ear, and a satchel of papers bigger than its chest.
prongs.habit: It recopies your notes at night and leaves both versions out, side by side.

finishes.name: Examiner's Clerk
finishes.of: one who has read every clause and can find it again
finishes.text: It has read every writ and remembers every clause. Houses lower their voices when it is in the room.
finishes.sign: A ledger chained to its belt, and a look over the top of spectacles it does not need.
finishes.habit: It files things. It has filed your socks.

finishes.name: Indexer
finishes.of: one who knows where everything is kept and what is missing
finishes.text: It knows what the Archive holds and where, and what is missing, and it suspects who.
finishes.sign: A dial on its chest turns to point at shelves. Its fingers are tabbed with coloured thread.
finishes.habit: It counts the spoons after every meal and looks at the door.

prongs.name: Ward-builder
prongs.of: one who stays behind to make it sound
prongs.text: It raises your wards where you point and stays inside them, patching, while you go on.
prongs.sign: A ring of chalk and cord hangs at its hip, and its knees are white with kneeling.
prongs.habit: It goes back to check the last thing it built, and then the one before.

finishes.name: Mason of the Post
finishes.of: one who leaves a place better walled than they found it
finishes.text: It has built a wall at every post you held. Some of them are still there. One has a door.
finishes.sign: Its forearms are faced with flat stone, and it carries a trowel worn to half its width.
finishes.habit: It restacks any loose stones it finds: a wall, a cairn, the rockery.

finishes.name: Maker's Maker
finishes.of: one who was taught and now teaches
finishes.text: It has begun making small ones of its own. They carry its tools and look at it the way it looked at you.
finishes.sign: Three little clay things on wheels follow it, carrying its tools and watching its hands.
finishes.habit: It shows the small ones how to hold a brush, with the patience you showed it.

prongs.name: Door-sitter
prongs.of: one who stays up until the work is put away
prongs.text: It does not sleep. It sits against the dormitory door with a lamp and counts the hours aloud, very quietly.
prongs.sign: It sits against the door with a lamp between its feet and its hands folded, very upright.
prongs.habit: It counts the hours aloud through the night, under its breath, and has not lost count.

finishes.name: Knocker-up
finishes.of: one who is awake first so that others are not caught asleep
finishes.text: It wakes the party before what is coming arrives. Nobody has worked out how it knows.
finishes.sign: One ear is larger than the other and cupped toward the window. It carries a long pole for tapping.
finishes.habit: It taps on each bedpost in turn a moment before the bell.

finishes.name: Hall's Caretaker
finishes.of: one who sweeps up after people who are no longer there
finishes.text: It sweeps the hearth where the shades sit and trims their lamp. They have told it how they were made.
finishes.sign: A broom of its own making and old, mild eyes. It steps round places where nobody is standing.
finishes.habit: It sweeps the hearth at the lamp hour and trims the wick the shades sit by.

paths.name: Likeness
paths.of: one who became themselves by copying someone they admired
paths.text: It learned from you so closely that it began to fight like you, and then to look like you.
paths.sign: It stands as you stand and has your way of holding its head. The face is nearly yours and not finished.
paths.habit: It practises your signature on scraps, and your walk in the corridor.

prongs.name: Sparring-doll
prongs.of: one who learned by being on the other end of it
prongs.text: It took every drill you did on the pell from the other side, and learned the answer to each.
prongs.sign: A smooth mask of a face, with dents where your practice blows fell.
prongs.habit: It stands in front of the pell at night and takes its place for a while.

finishes.name: Mirror-hand
finishes.of: one who has your habits so exactly that they answer for you
finishes.text: It parries as you parry, a half-beat after, from the foe's other side. The foe has not found a third side.
finishes.sign: Its guard hand is edged like yours and moves when yours does, as if on a string.
finishes.habit: It reaches for the cup with the same hand you do, at the same time, from across the table.

finishes.name: Pell-breaker
finishes.of: one who was hit until they understood hitting
finishes.text: It hits the way the training post taught it to be hit. It was listening the whole time.
finishes.sign: A thick ridge of fired clay over the brow, and knuckles like river stones.
finishes.habit: It leans its forehead against the training post, gently, before each session.

prongs.name: Clay Double
prongs.of: one who does the great thing second, and nearly as well
prongs.text: When your Pattern fires, it fires too, in clay. The second chain is slower and hits just as hard.
prongs.sign: A faint ring of your Pattern's light turns round its chest, a beat behind yours.
prongs.habit: It traces the figure of your Pattern in the air when it thinks you are asleep.

finishes.name: Walking Likeness
finishes.of: one who could pass for you and has never tried it on
finishes.text: At a distance your classmates cannot tell you apart. Nearer, it is the one not bleeding.
finishes.sign: It wears your face over its own. Up close you can see the join.
finishes.habit: It stands beside you at the mirror and corrects its expression to yours.

finishes.name: Sworn Likeness
finishes.of: one who took the same oath, on purpose, in their own voice
finishes.text: It took your oath beside you in its own voice. If you fall it will keep the Terms, and it has told you so.
finishes.sign: Your Terms are pressed into its chest in its own neat hand, under the glaze.
finishes.habit: It says the oath over each morning, and waits for you to say it too.

prongs.name: Clay Loader
prongs.of: one who has the next thing ready before it is asked for
prongs.text: It hands you the next shot before you reach for it, and has started taking the odd one itself.
prongs.sign: A lens set in one eye, and the next shot already in its open hand.
prongs.habit: It hands you things a moment before you reach: a pen, a spoon, your other boot.

finishes.name: Clay Sharpshooter
finishes.of: one who does not hurry and so does not miss
finishes.text: It never breathes, so it never has to hold a breath. It has not missed since it learned which end to point.
finishes.sign: One forearm has been made into a barrel. It does not breathe, and nothing about it moves.
finishes.habit: It sights along its arm at things across the yard and does not fire.

finishes.name: Brush-beater
finishes.of: one who cannot be frightened off a job
finishes.text: It walks into the brush clapping two stones and drives what you hunt onto your line. It cannot be frightened off.
finishes.sign: Long clay legs scratched to the hip by thorns, and a stone in each hand.
finishes.habit: It claps two stones together as it walks, and looks about to see what moves.

paths.name: Clay Bearer
paths.of: one who needs to be of use
paths.text: It learned from you that being made for a purpose is not the same as choosing one, and it chose yours.
paths.sign: Broad in the chest and bowed a little, as if something were already on its back.
paths.habit: It stands where it can be asked, and looks up whenever anyone sighs.

prongs.name: Fitter
prongs.of: one who cannot walk past a thing that is not working
prongs.text: It keeps the car's fittings and the post's lamp. It has a spanner your size and uses it one-handed.
prongs.sign: A spanner as long as your arm, carried one-handed. Small gears turn at its wrists.
prongs.habit: It tightens things as it passes: hinges, taps, the leg of your chair.

finishes.name: Master Fitter
finishes.of: one whose work does not need doing twice
finishes.text: No post it put right has gone dark again. The Compact has tried twice to hire it away from you.
finishes.sign: A brass plate on its chest is stamped with every post it has put right. There is room for more.
finishes.habit: It lays its tools out in order each evening and wipes each one.

finishes.name: Plate-layer
finishes.of: one who checks the road before the others travel it
finishes.text: It walks the rails ahead of the car tapping each with a hammer, and stops the car at the one that rings wrong.
finishes.sign: It walks with its feet set wide, as on a rail, and carries a long-handled hammer.
finishes.habit: It taps the flagstones along the corridor and stops on the loose one.

prongs.name: Clay Stand-in
prongs.of: one who believes they are easier to mend than you are
prongs.text: It steps into the blow because it can be mended and you cannot. It is right, and it is clay again by evening.
prongs.sign: Fresh grey clay over the chest where the last patch went in, still drying.
prongs.habit: It presses its own cracks shut with a thumb, and looks to see if you noticed.

finishes.name: Thrice-mended
finishes.of: one who is more repair than original, and proud of the repairs
finishes.text: More patch than clay now. Every repair is your work, and it keeps each one where you can see it.
finishes.sign: More rivet and patch than clay. Each mend is left unpainted, where it shows.
finishes.habit: It runs a finger along its seams in the order they were made.

finishes.name: Kiln-fired
finishes.of: one who went through the fire by accident and came out certain
finishes.text: Your fire went through it once by accident. It rang when it cooled, and nothing has cracked it since.
finishes.sign: Fired hard and dark, with a glaze crazed like old porcelain. It rings if you tap it.
finishes.habit: It stands close to the stove, closer than anyone should, and is at ease there.

prongs.name: Pack-porter
prongs.of: one who carries it and does not ask what it is
prongs.text: It carries what the party cannot. It has never asked what is in the packs.
prongs.sign: Strap-plates across both shoulders and a carrying-band worn into its brow.
prongs.habit: It picks up whatever has been set down by the door and waits beside it.

finishes.name: Litter-bearer
finishes.of: one who carries the one who cannot walk, and does not spill a cup
finishes.text: When the passenger cannot walk it carries them, at a pace that would not spill a cup.
finishes.sign: Arms made long and flat for carrying, held a little out from its sides.
finishes.habit: It walks the corridor at night with a full cup, practising.

finishes.name: Cohort's Hand
finishes.of: one who is there with the right thing and gone before the thanks
finishes.text: Every one of your classmates has been handed the right thing by it at the right moment, and not seen it arrive.
finishes.sign: Its palms glow a little, and whatever you needed is already in them.
finishes.habit: It leaves things at the foot of the right bed: a mended strap, a dry sock.
